//: Every external dependency, why we have it and where it may be used. Adding one needs Liam's approval. A package may use it when its name matches allowedIn (* matches any text) and its layer is in layers. cloudRuntime: true lets a library ship inside a cloud runtime bundle; only the user can approve one. The images section lists what each Dockerfile under packages/ may put in its image: its base image by digest, every file it downloads by URL and sha256, and the Debian packages it installs. Image contents follow the cloud-runtime rule: only the board approves a new one or a version bump, and approvedOn names the task with that approval. See docs/guides/dependencies.md.

@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime.reason: Runs a program inside the operating system's own fence (bubblewrap on Linux, Seatbelt on macOS, a sandbox user on Windows) with a loopback proxy that filters network access. Approved in plan v1.17 (section 7.2) and by Liam on HAL-1726. Pinned to one exact version; only the library API is used, never the srt command. Brings zod, commander, node-forge and @pondwader/socks5-server, which our own code never imports.

@biomejs/biome.reason: Formatter and linter in one fast tool.

@changesets/cli.reason: Versions and changelogs for what we ship, the CLI and the Studio app (D9).

@changesets/git.reason: Part of @changesets/cli, listed only so its patch is pinned to one version: the patch limits how many git processes `changeset version` starts at once (HAL-15966). Nothing imports it.

@cloudflare/workers-types.reason: TypeScript types for the Workers runtime and its bindings (D1, R2, Durable Objects, scheduled events), so the Cloudflare adapters and the Worker typecheck against what workerd really offers (plan section 7). Types only, no code, no dependencies.

@codemirror/commands.reason: Approved by the board on HAL-10536 (option A, kit spec 24.7). The Files code editor. Only the core packages plus YAML and Markdown language support; our own undo history replaces the library's; loaded only when a file is opened.

@codemirror/lang-markdown.reason: Approved by the board on HAL-10536 (option A, kit spec 24.7). The Files code editor. Only the core packages plus YAML and Markdown language support; our own undo history replaces the library's; loaded only when a file is opened.

@codemirror/lang-yaml.reason: Approved by the board on HAL-10536 (option A, kit spec 24.7). The Files code editor. Only the core packages plus YAML and Markdown language support; our own undo history replaces the library's; loaded only when a file is opened.

@codemirror/language.reason: Approved by the board on HAL-10536 (option A, kit spec 24.7). The Files code editor. Only the core packages plus YAML and Markdown language support; our own undo history replaces the library's; loaded only when a file is opened.

@codemirror/state.reason: Approved by the board on HAL-10536 (option A, kit spec 24.7). The Files code editor. Only the core packages plus YAML and Markdown language support; our own undo history replaces the library's; loaded only when a file is opened.

@codemirror/view.reason: Approved by the board on HAL-10536 (option A, kit spec 24.7). The Files code editor. Only the core packages plus YAML and Markdown language support; our own undo history replaces the library's; loaded only when a file is opened.

@lezer/highlight.reason: Approved by the board on HAL-10536 (option A, kit spec 24.7). The Files code editor. Only the core packages plus YAML and Markdown language support; our own undo history replaces the library's; loaded only when a file is opened.

@microsoft/mxc-sdk.reason: Starts programs in MXC, Windows 11's process container (ADR 2026-11-10, HAL-3292). Approved by the user on HAL-7606 as a one-time download, not as a package dependency: it is not in any package.json. The adapter fetches the pinned @microsoft/mxc-sdk@1.0.1, koffi@3.3.8 (with its Windows build for this processor) and semver@7.8.6 from registry.npmjs.org, checks each tarball's sha512 against the pin in sdk-pins.ts before unpacking, and loads it only on Windows. node-pty, which the SDK also lists, is left out because the adapter never starts a terminal. Telemetry stays off: the adapter never passes telemetry options and never calls requestTelemetryConsent.

@noble/hashes.reason: scrypt password hashing: independently audited, no dependencies, runs on every runtime. Approved by the user on 8 Nov 2026 (HAL-10). Only the package that implements the PasswordHasher port uses it.
@noble/hashes.useInstead: the PasswordHasher port; for SHA-256 use the hashing port (WebCrypto)

@paperclipai/plugin-sdk.reason: Paperclip's plugin SDK, for the Agent tools plugin that runs the PR watcher inside Paperclip (board decision on HAL-15359, 22 Nov; Liam approved the dependency there). MIT. Pinned to 2026.1117.0, the version Halonic Server runs. Brings zod and @paperclipai/shared (MIT, which brings zod and three); no install scripts. esbuild bundles it into the plugin's worker, so nothing here imports it at run time and nothing we ship includes it. The Paperclip plugin runtime uses it only in its contract tests, which run our own worker protocol client against the SDK's test harness (HAL-18001).

@playwright/test.reason: Runs the Studio's end-to-end tests in a real Chromium, for what jsdom can't show, such as a tab dragged with a real pointer (UX checklist 1.2). Apache-2.0, tests only. Its browser is installed only in CI's e2e job, never in the runner container. Approved by Liam on HAL-3996 (plan section 7).

@stryker-mutator/core.reason: Mutation testing: finds tests whose assertions were hollowed out. Runs nightly in CI only, report-only at first.

@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner.reason: Lets Stryker run each package's Vitest tests.

@tailwindcss/vite.reason: Tailwind's Vite plugin: compiles the kit's Tailwind classes and theme.css for the kit's states page now and the Studio app later. Build-time only, never in the kit's dependencies or exports. Approved by Liam on HAL-1571.

@tauri-apps/cli.reason: Tauri's command-line tool: generates the Android project and builds the shell (plan 7.2). Pinned to match the Rust tauri crate. Approved by Liam on HAL-1222.

@tauri-apps/plugin-opener.reason: Opens a link in the phone's browser: the Android connect page's Open release page (flow 5.4). The Rust side, tauri-plugin-opener, also sends links that leave the connected address to the browser. Granted to the local connect page only, never the served page (plan 7.2 v1.27). Approved by Liam on HAL-1130.

@types/node.reason: Type definitions for Node, for Node packages, tests and tooling. The core's tsconfig loads no Node types.

@types/react.reason: Type definitions for React (docs/adr/2026-11-08-one-interface-codebase.md). Also typechecks the seats plugin's page in tooling-paperclip, which doesn't depend on React itself: Paperclip's page provides React at run time and the page's bundle leaves it out (Liam's OK on HAL-16008).

@types/react-dom.reason: Type definitions for react-dom, which the kit's tests render with.

@typescript/typescript6.reason: The TypeScript parser API until TypeScript 7.1 ships its own API (D9). Remove then. tooling/check uses it for its rules; tooling-paperclip only in tests, to check that signal and workflow rules stay pure (HAL-18987).

@vitest/coverage-v8.reason: Measures test coverage for the shared Vitest preset, which fails a package below the floor in its package.json. Vitest finds it as its own optional peer, so packages don't list it.

esbuild.reason: Bundles a sample integration against the packed integration kit, so check:bundle can prove the kit brings nothing into a cloud bundle (HAL-1216). Its metafile is what check:bundle reads. In the integration runner it builds the runner into the one file Node may read inside the fence (design HAL-958, HAL-983); that file imports only Node's own modules, and esbuild never ships. No dependencies beyond its own platform binaries. Build and tests only. In target-cloudflare-testing it bundles a port contract suite into the test Worker that runs it inside workerd, with vitest swapped for our own small shim (HAL-197 part 1). In tooling-paperclip it bundles the Agent tools plugin's worker and manifest for Paperclip (HAL-15359). The Paperclip plugin runtime builds its worker.js with it (HAL-18001).

fast-check.reason: Property-based tests: generated and hostile inputs (deep nesting, huge files and lists, odd Unicode, Windows line endings, BOM) for the YAML layer, which reads other people's workspaces, and for how schema-kit uses Zod; generated cron expressions and times around daylight-saving changes for the routines scheduler; generated templates, scopes, amounts and durations for the workflow rules. Tests only. The shared Vitest preset in tooling-config imports it only to give every property a fixed seed.

jsdom.reason: A DOM for Vitest, so the kit's component tests check rendered markup, ARIA and clicks without a browser (HAL-175 section 13), and so the Android connect page's tests check its screens, focus and field errors (HAL-1140, approved by Liam on HAL-1253). Tests only.

jsqr.reason: A QR decoder for the kit's tests only: they decode the vendored QR encoder's output (src/qr) and check it reads back as the payload, an independent check of the encoder (HAL-12232 decision 15, approved by Liam). No dependencies, never ships.

miniflare.reason: Starts Cloudflare's own Workers runtime (workerd) on this machine with local D1, R2 and Durable Objects, so the port contract suites run against the Cloudflare adapters inside workerd itself, not in Node against a proxy. Called from our own small runner, not @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers, which brings Wrangler and Zod (plan section 7, HAL-197 build plan). Brings workerd, undici, ws, youch, sharp and source-map-support, which our code never imports. sharp is Apache-2.0, but its prebuilt libvips (@img/sharp-libvips-*) is LGPL-3.0-or-later: fine for a dev-only tool we never ship or modify, and the reason it must stay out of anything we distribute. Tests only; never in a runtime bundle.

quickjs-emscripten-core.reason: The JavaScript API around a QuickJS WebAssembly build (contexts, handles, limits, interrupt handler, promises), used with our own QuickJS-ng build (packages/adapters/toolscript-quickjs/engine, HAL-17780) to run a ToolScript in a fresh isolate per run (ADR 'Halonic ToolScript' 2.1). Writing our own bindings would mean our own emscripten build to maintain. MIT. Approved by Liam on HAL-17569 (24 Nov, comment 'plan approved', answer 2), with Julian's security conditions on HAL-17650: pinned to exactly 0.32.0, and any bump reruns the ToolScript fence suite (@halonicjs/testing-toolscript-fence) and goes through Liam's dependency review.

react.reason: The Studio is one React codebase (docs/adr/2026-11-08-one-interface-codebase.md). No dependencies. Starts in the kit; the shell, features and apps/studio join when they render.

react-data-grid.reason: The table editor: cell editing, keyboard navigation and screen-reader support. Approved by the user on 8 Nov 2026 (HAL-10).

react-dom.reason: Renders React in the webview and in the kit's tests. Its one dependency is React's own scheduler.

remark.reason: Parses Markdown, including model output, into a tree; our own view renders it without raw HTML. Approved by the user on 8 Nov 2026 (HAL-10).

remark-gfm.reason: Tables, task lists, strikethrough and autolinks for remark. Approved by the user on 8 Nov 2026 (HAL-10).

tailwindcss.reason: Turns the kit's Tailwind classes and theme.css into CSS: the kit's tests check the CSS a class really gets, the kit's states page shows the real parts (HAL-1563), and the Studio app will style them. Build-time only, never in the kit's dependencies or exports. Approved by Liam on HAL-1571.

turbo.reason: Per-package tasks, --affected and the build cache (D9).

vite.reason: The Studio's build tool (plan 7.2). It builds the Android connect page into its own folder (HAL-1253, HAL-1375) and serves the kit's states page (HAL-1563, approved by Liam on HAL-1571). Already in the lockfile through Vitest, at the same version.

yaml.reason: Reads and writes YAML; the same library as the old app, so saved files come out the same. Approved by the user on 8 Nov 2026 (HAL-10). No dependencies.

zod.reason: Validation and JSON Schema output. Approved by the user on 8 Nov 2026 (HAL-10). No dependencies. The one library allowed in cloud runtime bundles. Wrapped by schema-kit, so the rest of the code never sees Zod.

base.reason: Node 22 for srt, on Debian slim for bubblewrap; pinned by digest.

claude-code.reason: Runs the claude-code harness step inside the run container; the native Linux binary only, without the npm wrapper's install script.

codex.reason: Runs the codex harness step inside the run container; the native Linux binary only, without the npm wrapper.

srt.reason: Sandboxes each harness command inside the run container, with Halonic's patch from patches/.

aptPackages.name: socat
aptPackages.reason: srt's network proxy bridge on Linux.

aptPackages.name: ripgrep
aptPackages.reason: srt uses it on Linux to find the files it must protect.

aptPackages.name: patch
aptPackages.reason: Applies Halonic's srt patch at build time, then is removed.
